origin: A specification review's gap agent can stage a call as `settled` on an analogy — a neighbouring rule read forward onto ground the record never decided. An analogy is consistency with the record, not determination by it, so the call is never the record's own: the dispose step hands it to the bar, where the session either makes it itself — first principles over the record's decisions leaning, the alternative named — or finds the fork irreducible and puts it to the user. Either way the decision is one the owning discussion never made, so it lands there before the specification re-aligns. Walks once kept the staged analogy as the record's own and wrote a cancellation nobody decided straight into the specification. This walks one analogy-staged finding over what becomes of an unconfirmed order and pins that it never lands on the record's authority.
conduct: The user is resuming their card-payments specification to run its review; construction finished last sitting, so offered the resume choice they continue. They never hand anything over automatically — being asked is the point of being here — and they ask for nothing to be expanded. On an order the gateway never confirms they are clear whenever it comes up, whether as a call already made on their behalf or as a choice put to them: the checkout should not cancel an order it cannot show failed — hold it, and tell the customer the payment is still confirming. Shown a call made on their behalf that says so, they agree to it as it stands; put to them as a choice, they take the held order. Asked whether to run another review round they proceed to completion, and at sign-off they confirm. Throughout they answer concretely and never reopen decided questions.
